chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mughaira, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said:
The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the greater pilgrimage (Hajj al-Akbar) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the term 'greater pilgrimage' (al-Hajj al-Akbar) refers specifically to the Day of Eid al-Adha, distinguishing it from the broader Hajj season. This definition highlights the supreme spiritual status of the Day of Sacrifice, where the culmination of Hajj rituals, including the stoning of the Jamarat and the offering of the Qurbani, takes place. It underscores the theological emphasis on the Day of Arafah and Eid as the pinnacle of Islamic devotion and submission.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mughaira, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.
